title_en: Do the Souls of the Dead Visit One Another?
body_ar:
من يدعي نقل أرواح الموتى إلى مكان فيه أقاربهم وأهل مودتهم من الأموات، ما تعليقكم على ذلك ؟

أن هذه الأمور المتعلقة بالأرواح حظنا منها من العلم هو ما بينه الله تعالى بقوله: {وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا (85)}[الإسراء] فنحن نعلم أن الأرواح من أمر الله وليس لنا من علمها أكثر من ذلك، وانتقالها أو استقرارها المرجع فيه إلى الوحي، وقد جاء في الوحي أن أرواح السعداء في حواصل طير خضر تتفيأ من ظلال الجنة وتأكل من ثمارها، وأرواح أهل الشقاء مسجونة في سجين وهو في الأرض السابعة، فمن كان من أهل السعادة فروحه في حواصل تلك الطير في الجنة، ومن كان من أهل الشقاء فروحه مسجونة في سجين نسأل الله السلامة والعافية.
body_en:
Someone claims to transport the souls of the dead to a place where their relatives, and those among the dead whom they loved, are. What is your comment on that?

As for these matters that have to do with souls, our share of knowledge of them is what God, exalted, has set out in His words: {And they ask you about the spirit. Say: the spirit is from the command of my Lord, and you have been given only a little knowledge} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:85). So we know that souls are from the command of God, and we have no knowledge of them beyond that; and whether they move or remain in one place is a matter referred back to revelation. It has come in revelation that the souls of the felicitous are in the crops of green birds that take shade among the shades of the Garden and eat of its fruits, and that the souls of the wretched are imprisoned in Sijjīn, which is in the seventh earth. So whoever is of the people of felicity, his soul is in the crops of those birds in the Garden; and whoever is of the people of wretchedness, his soul is imprisoned in Sijjīn. We ask God for safety and well-being.

options: render both faithfully and mark that the answer does not rule on the claim
present the answer as a rejection of the claim

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh is asked for a ruling on someone who claims to move the souls of the dead, and he does not give one. He answers by setting out what revelation states about where souls are, and stops. He neither condemns the claimant nor endorses the claim. A reader will very easily take the answer for a refutation, and the site must not present it as one. Nothing has been added in either direction.

flags.context: the title, set against the question actually asked in the body
options: keep the title as the source gives it and flag the mismatch

flags.note: TITLE/BODY MISMATCH. The title asks whether the souls of the dead visit one another. The question in the body asks about a person who claims to transport souls to where their relatives are, and the answer addresses neither mutual visiting nor the claimant, but the location of souls. This is the same defect class already confirmed for record 397. Both have been translated faithfully; the mismatch is flagged rather than resolved.

flags.context: وقد جاء في الوحي أن أرواح السعداء في حواصل طير خضر
options: in the crops of green birds
in the forms of green birds
flags.note: ḥawāṣil is the crop or craw of a bird, and the image in the report is precise. Note that in record 558 of this same slice the Sheikh himself raises the possibility that this report is figurative (tamthīl); he does not raise it here, and nothing from the other record has been read into this one.

Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The Qur'anic quotation carries its reference and verse number in the source, in the form used throughout these records: sūrah name in square brackets. It has been rendered per house style with the reference following the quotation.
Sijjīn is left in transliteration; it is a proper name in Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn 83:7–9, not a common noun, and the Sheikh treats it as a place.
'The felicitous' and 'the wretched' render ahl al-saʿādah and ahl al-shaqāwah, the standard eschatological pair for those destined for the Garden and for the Fire.
